newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Iliescu pardons ex-communists ahead of handover.
newsitem.headline: Iliescu pardons ex-communists ahead of handover.

text.p: Romanian President Ion Iliescu has signed a decree to pardon six former Communist Party bosses before stepping down this week after seven years in power.

The pardons, reported by Mediafax news agency late on Wednesday, were extended to top aides of executed dictator Nicolae Ceausescu, including his ideology chief, who had been convicted of mass murder and communist-era abuse of power.
The pardons were signed last week but were not immediately announced. State television reported the decree and read out the names of those pardoned without any comment.
"Iliescu's decree marks the finale of the scenario of the so-called anti-communist revolution," Ticu Dumitrescu, head of an association of former political prisoners, told Reuters.
"Former communists like Iliescu, who ruled for seven years, had no real reason to keep their former colleagues in jail."
Iliescu, who took power after the 1989 upheaval that ousted Ceausescu, hands over to centrist Emil Constantinescu, who is to be sworn in as president on Friday.
Iliescu is expected to host the president-elect at the presidential Cotroceni palace on Thursday to discuss the last details of the handover, sources close to Constantinescu said.

Constantinescu, who had no political career under communism, defeated the veteran leader in this month's presidential election. Iliescu's leftist party was thrown out of office in general elections held two weeks earlier.
The pardons covered Ceausescu's ideologist Dumitru Popescu, who was behind the dictator's policies in his final years and earned the nickname "God" because of his stern attitudes.
Other beneficiaries were Lina Ciobanu, Nicolae Constantin, Constantin Olteanu, Gheorghe Oprea and Gheorghe Pana -- all members of the defunct Communist Party's Politburo.

All had been convicted in connection with attempts to suppress 1989 demonstrations against Ceausescu which culminated in his capture and execution. Several lesser-known figures also received pardons as did two journalists convicted of libel.

None of the six was in jail. All had been freed on health grounds over the past four years, along with 10 other Politburo members jailed in 1991 on similar charges. More than 1,000 Romanians were killed during the upheaval seven years ago.
Iliescu made no mention of the pardons when he outlined his record in office at his final news conference on Tuesday.
Two and a half years ago he had pardoned eight of the 16 Politburo members originally convicted.

A former Ceausescu aide, Iliescu insists that the events seven years ago, during which more than 1,000 people were killed, were a genuine revolution. Critics call it a plot masterminded by Iliescu and his entourage to topple Ceausescu and keep power for themselves.
